causes.text: On April 1, 2024, the U.S. Postal Service selected UPS as its primary air cargo provider, replacing FedEx after more than 20 years. Reuters noted that UPS would handle most of the Postal Service's air mail contract, valued at roughly $2 billion annually, while FedEx's shares fell nearly 2% on the announcement. Losing the USPS contract meant FedEx faced a significant hit to high-margin express volumes.

source_info.title: UPS to replace FedEx as U.S. Postal Service's primary air cargo provider

effects.text: On September 20, 2024, FedEx reported a sharp drop in quarterly profit as weak demand and customers' shift to slower, cheaper deliveries hammered its express segment. Reuters described how cost savings fell short of expectations and noted that shares plunged more than 15%, wiping out about $11 billion in market value. The loss of high-margin USPS volumes earlier in the year compounded the weakness in priority shipments and contributed to the profit decline.

source_info.title: FedEx shares tumble over 15% on limp demand, delivery trade-down

causal_reasoning_chain.description: USPS's move to UPS removed a long-standing stream of high-margin express volume from FedEx's air network, increasing fixed-cost burden per package and pressuring margins.
That lost volume coincided with softer demand and a shift to slower, cheaper services, limiting FedEx's ability to backfill premium express revenue despite cost-cutting.
When FedEx reported results on 2024-09-20, the compounded effects manifested in a profit shortfall and a 15% stock drop, reflecting concerns about sustained pressure on the express air network.

rationale: Losing USPS's primary air contract removed high-margin express volume just as the market softened, amplifying margin compression and culminating in a steep equity sell-off when results were disclosed.
counterfactual_analysis: If UPS had not won the USPS contract, FedEx would likely have retained meaningful premium volume, cushioning utilization and margins; the reported profit decline and stock reaction would probably have been less severe.

adversarial_confounders.text: Broader economic slowdown reducing shipping volumes.
adversarial_confounders.impact: Could depress FedEx profits regardless of the USPS contract loss.
Higher operating costs could compress margins independent of volume shifts.

details.pestel_factor: Economic - Express volume contraction and shift to lower-cost services
details.commentary: The Postal Service's rebidding of its air-cargo contract reflected shifting government procurement priorities and heightened price sensitivity. When that high-margin business moved to UPS, the broader customer shift toward cheaper, slower shipping options intensified the pressure on FedEx's express economics.

USPS demonstrated how a large, concentrated customer can wield significant buyer power in the express market. Its decision to switch providers exposed FedEx's dependence on a single account and weakened its competitive position in priority air freight.

Losing the USPS volumes raised unit costs across FedEx's express network just as demand was softening. The resulting profit shortfall undermined investor confidence, reinforcing a negative spiral in which weaker results made it harder to justify the fixed-cost base, driving the stock sharply lower.
